result.rationale: The diff adds the 'add_members' menu item unconditionally in BookingListItem.tsx ({ id: "add_members", label: t("additional_guests") ... }) with no conditional gating, while addGuests.handler.ts enforces FORBIDDEN for users who are not team admin/owner, organizer, or attendee. The described mechanism is verifiable: unrelated users would see the action and hit the error only after submitting. This is a real, specific scope/UX concern (ungated UI vs. server-side authorization), not a correctness defect since the server properly rejects.

judged_text: The 'additional_guests' menu option is added unconditionally to every booking item with no gating on booking state (past/cancelled bookings) or the user's role, even though the handler will reject FORBIDDEN for unrelated users. Users browsing bookings where they are neither organizer, attendee, nor team owner see the Add Guests action, open the dialog, enter emails, and only then receive a FORBIDDEN toast — work the diff ships that is not traceable to the intended audience of the feature.

adjudication.rationale: In `BookingListItem.tsx`, the new action `{ id: "add_members", label: t("additional_guests"), onClick: () => setIsOpenAddGuestsDialog(true) }` is appended to `actions` unconditionally (no checks on booking status/time or user role). The TRPC handler (`addGuests.handler.ts`) does enforce authorization and can throw `FORBIDDEN` when the user is not team admin/owner, organizer, or attendee, meaning the UI can expose an action that will predictably fail for some viewers. This is a real, diff-grounded UX/scope issue (feature discoverability/audience), not a security defect because the server-side guard exists.
